scheme_name: Scheme of Assistance for Common Environment Infrastructure: Common Boiler Project by SPV Constituted by Minimum 10 MSMEs
description:
The Scheme of Assistance for Common Environment Infrastructure is a significant initiative launched by the Government of India to promote environmental sustainability and support Micro Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). 

This scheme was officially launched in 2020 as part of the broader efforts to enhance the environmental infrastructure in industrial clusters across the country. 

The initiative is particularly focused on providing assistance for the establishment of common boiler facilities. 

The common boiler project is designed to cater to a minimum of ten MSMEs that are located in close proximity to each other. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to reduce the environmental impact of industrial operations by promoting the use of cleaner technologies. 

The scheme aims to facilitate the establishment of common boiler facilities that will help in reducing emissions and improving energy efficiency. 

The target is to establish at least 100 common boiler projects across various industrial clusters by the year 2025. 

The benefits of this scheme include financial assistance for the establishment of common boiler facilities. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme can go up to 50% of the project cost. 

The maximum limit for financial assistance is set at INR 50 lakhs per project. 

This means that if the total project cost is INR 1 crore, the eligible MSMEs can receive up to INR 50 lakhs as assistance from the government. 

Additionally, the scheme aims to provide technical support and guidance to MSMEs in the planning and execution of these projects. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are specifically tailored to MSMEs. 

To qualify, an enterprise must be classified as an MSME according to the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act of 2006. 

This classification is based on the investment in plant and machinery or equipment. 

For micro enterprises, the investment limit is up to INR 1 crore. 

For small enterprises, the investment limit is between INR 1 crore and INR 10 crores. 

For medium enterprises, the investment limit is between INR 10 crores and INR 50 crores. 

Furthermore, the participating MSMEs must be located within the same industrial cluster. 

They must also demonstrate a commitment to adopting cleaner technologies and practices. 

The application process for the Scheme of Assistance for Common Environment Infrastructure is structured and requires several steps. 

First, the interested MSMEs must form a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV). 

This SPV must consist of at least ten MSMEs that are willing to collaborate on the common boiler project. 

Once the SPV is formed, the members must prepare a detailed project proposal. 

This proposal should outline the project objectives, expected outcomes, and a clear budget. 

The proposal must also include an environmental impact assessment to demonstrate the project's benefits. 

The next step involves submitting the project proposal to the respective State Pollution Control Board (SPCB). 

The SPCB will review the proposal and assess its compliance with environmental regulations. 

If the proposal is approved, it will be forwarded to the Ministry of Micro Small and Medium Enterprises for further processing. 

The required documents for the application include the SPV formation documents, project proposal, environmental clearance, and financial statements of the participating MSMEs. 

The timeline for the entire application process can vary but typically takes around 3 to 6 months from the submission of the proposal to the disbursement of funds. 

The disbursement of financial assistance is usually made in installments based on the progress of the project. 

The first installment is generally released after the approval of the project proposal. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the completion of specific milestones outlined in the project plan. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Micro Small and Medium Enterprises. 

The ministry works in collaboration with the State Pollution Control Boards to ensure the effective implementation of the scheme. 

Contact details for the Ministry of MSME can be found on their official website. 

They provide a dedicated helpline for MSMEs seeking assistance with the application process. 

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of capacity building and training for the participating MSMEs. 

Workshops and training sessions are organized to educate MSMEs about best practices in environmental management. 

The government aims to create awareness about the benefits of adopting cleaner technologies among MSMEs. 

Statistically, the scheme is expected to contribute to a significant reduction in industrial emissions. 

It is projected that the establishment of common boiler facilities will lead to a decrease in carbon emissions by approximately 20% in the participating MSMEs. 

Furthermore, the scheme is aligned with the Government of India's commitment to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals. 

It specifically addresses Goal 12 which focuses on ensuring sustainable consumption and production patterns. 

The initiative is also expected to create job opportunities in the environmental management sector. 

By promoting cleaner technologies, the scheme aims to enhance the competitiveness of MSMEs in the global market. 

The government has allocated a budget of INR 500 crores for the implementation of this scheme over the next five years. 

This funding is intended to support the establishment of common infrastructure that will benefit multiple MSMEs. 

The scheme is a part of the larger Make in India initiative which aims to boost manufacturing in the country. 

By providing financial assistance and technical support, the government is encouraging MSMEs to invest in sustainable practices. 

The common boiler project is expected to enhance energy efficiency and reduce operational costs for participating MSMEs. 

In conclusion, the Scheme of Assistance for Common Environment Infrastructure is a pivotal initiative aimed at promoting environmental sustainability among MSMEs. 

With specific financial assistance, eligibility criteria, and a structured application process, the scheme is designed to facilitate the establishment of common boiler facilities. 

This initiative not only aims to reduce emissions but also enhances the overall competitiveness of MSMEs in India. 

By fostering collaboration among MSMEs, the scheme is expected to create a significant impact on the industrial landscape of the country.
